Psychedelic-assisted psychotherapy (PAP) is an emerging intervention applied to a variety of psychiatric disorders (Schenberg, 2018). In PAP, a supportive psychotherapy regimen is combined with classic psychedelics such as psilocybin or lysergic acid diethylamide (LSD) (Reiff et al., 2020). Psilocybin is a naturally occurring psychedelic compound predominantly found in the Psilocybe genus of mushrooms (Sacks et al., 2018). Psilocybin is classified as a classic serotonergic psychedelic, as extant literature suggests that the hallucinogenic effect of psilocybin is mediated by agonism of the serotonergic 5-hydroxytryptamine 2A receptor (5-HT2ARs) by psilocin, the active metabolite of psilocybin (Ling et al., 2022).
In particular, PAP has been investigated as an intervention for mood disorders, obsessive-compulsive disorder (Moreno, Wiegand, Taitano, & Delgado, 2006), and alcohol and tobacco use disorders (Bogenschutz et al., 2015; Johnson, Garcia-Romeu, Cosimano, & Griffiths, 2014). Past studies have primarily focused on determining the therapeutic efficacy of PAP in patients with depressive symptoms (Coppola, Bevione, & Mondola, 2022). Several reviews and meta-analyses of PAP for depression have been previously completed based on small initial pilot trials (Galvão-Coelho et al., 2021; Goldberg et al., 2020; Reiff et al., 2020; Romeo, Karila, Martelli, & Benyamina, 2020).
Trials to date have typically excluded participants with complex presentations. Our aim was to determine the feasibility of PAP in a complex population, including high levels of treatment resistance in major depressive and bipolar disorder and patients with baseline suicidality and significant comorbidity.
Large effect sizes were observed in the overall sample and following subgroup analyses by diagnosis and control method in nine clinical trials comprising 340 psilocybin-treated participants. PAP administration resulted in a significantly greater antidepressant effect at the primary endpoint from baseline · In this systematic review and meta-analysis examining the antidepressant effects of PAP in patients with MDD or LTC, psilocybin was found to have a significantly greater antidepressant effect compared to the comparator arms.
